analysis.lean: No strong edge: the blended number (OKC -9.2) sits almost on the market (OKC -9.5), so this is a pass, with a slight tilt to Phoenix +9.5 only if you trust the raw ratings.
why: Ratings projection is OKC +5.9 against a market of -9.5. That is 3.6 points of gap in Phoenix's favor, but it rests on 2 PHX games and 3 OKC games, so it is mostly noise.

Opponent-adjusted net is OKC +2.4 versus PHX -2.6 per 100 possessions, and both are shrunk toward average. Raw scoring is far more extreme (OKC allows 96.3 per game, PHX allows 123.0), and I would not lean on that.
Rest favors Phoenix: OKC is on a back-to-back and PHX has 1 day off. That is a real factor, but it is small and the line likely already prices it, so I made no adjustment.
Total: the model says 222.8 and the market is 218.5, so the blend lands at 218.8. Both teams are at 103.7 adjusted pace, and the raw 107.0 and 106.7 points per game do not argue for a change.
Phoenix has allowed a 37.2% offensive rebound rate in 2 games, while OKC forces turnovers on 19.9% of possessions. Those are tiny samples, but they point to extra OKC possessions.
risks: Jalen Williams (ankle, stretchered off, Day-To-Day), Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams are all unresolved for OKC. If Williams is out, the spread could move and OKC's depth is thin, since Topic, Sorber and Oweh are also out.
A big spread plus a back-to-back raises blowout risk: starters could sit in the fourth quarter, which hurts star player overs.
Phoenix's two results are wildly different (W 131-122, L 83-124), so the sample says little about what to expect.
matchups: Mark Williams is Out and Oso Ighodaro is doubtful, so Phoenix is thin at center. Khaman Maluach (22.5 min, 7.5 reb) would carry the load against Holmgren and Hartenstein.
Booker averages 33.0 points on 32.5 minutes, so Phoenix's offense depends heavily on him. OKC's defense has allowed only 96.3 per game in 3 games, which is a small sample.

analysis.lean: Lean Denver at home, but the market (-7.5) is already above our ratings projection (+4.2), so there is little edge and no reason to move the line.
why: Our ratings projection is Denver +4.2 and the market is -7.5. The blended number (+7.3) leans almost entirely on the market because the ratings weight is only 0.07.
GSW is 0-3 with a raw 111.7 scored / 123.0 allowed per game. Its opponent-adjusted net is only -2.4 per 100 because of early-season shrinkage, so the raw results look worse than the adjusted rating.
DEN is 1-1 with an adjusted net of -0.5. The sample is two games, which includes a 141-135 win and an 84-96 loss, so the rating is weak evidence.
GSW's defense allowed an opponent eFG of 0.617 over 3 games, and its TOV% forced is 0.191. The first is a poor defensive number, the second a good one, and both come from a tiny sample.

Both teams are on 1 day of rest, so there is no rest mismatch to justify an adjustment. The total of 234.5 sits above our 229.6, but the projection's pace (103.8) matches the market's implied pace, so I have no quantified reason to move it.
risks: The sample is 2-3 games per team, so every rating and four-factor number is noisy.
Santos (GSW) is questionable, Diallo and Johnson (DEN) are doubtful, and the late status of these players could move the line before tip.
matchups: Jokic has a rebounding and passing edge against a thin GSW frontcourt that is missing Porzingis (out), though Horford and Bassey are available (from memory: roster/role details may be outdated).
Curry (23.5 pts per game in the data) is GSW's main scoring source, and Butler and Moody are out, so GSW's creation is thin.
verify: Confirm Santos's status (questionable, left knee) and whether Bassey and B. Williams (both probable) play.
Confirm Diallo and Johnson (both doubtful) are out for DEN.
Check for line movement from -7.5 and 234.5 and shop other books for a better number.
Moneyline prices were not loaded, so the price cannot be checked.
